alerts.title: DTG-associated weight gain and metabolic deterioration
alerts.message: Guidelines note DTG is well-tolerated but hyperglycemia in non-diabetics has been reported. Patient gained 17kg (65→82kg, BMI 25.6→32.4) over 18 months on DTG, with new impaired fasting glucose (118 mg/dL), HbA1c 6.1%, dyslipidaemia (LDL 148, TG 212), acanthosis nigricans, and BP rise (118/74→138/88). She has ≥2 hyperglycemia risk factors: age ≥30, BMI ≥25, and family history of DM. Guidelines state clients with ≥2 risk factors need glucose monitoring every 3 months for 12 months after DTG initiation. Evidence for DTG attribution: temporal relationship with weight gain and metabolic changes after switch. Against: EFV may also cause dyslipidaemia; lifestyle factors unknown. No clinician plan was documented today.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess for DTG-related metabolic toxicity. Consider lifestyle intervention, weight management, and evaluate whether DTG continuation is appropriate given progressive metabolic syndrome. Document a formal plan.

alerts.title: Missing glucose monitoring per DTG risk-factor protocol
alerts.message: Guidelines require RBS/FBS every 3 months for the first 12 months in clients with ≥2 hyperglycemia risk factors on DTG. This patient had ≥3 risk factors (age ≥30, BMI ≥25, family history of DM) at DTG transition 18 months ago, but no prior glucose monitoring results are recorded. The first documented glucose (118 mg/dL) and HbA1c (6.1%) appear only now, well outside the recommended 3-monthly monitoring window. This represents a missed opportunity for early detection of DTG-associated hyperglycemia.

evidence.recommended_action: Establish ongoing glucose monitoring (FBS or HbA1c) at appropriate intervals. Screen for diabetes given current pre-diabetic range results and reinforce lifestyle counselling.

alerts.title: No clinician assessment or plan documented
alerts.message: Guidelines emphasise integrated screening for HIV and NCD comorbidities at each clinic visit. This patient presents with significant metabolic abnormalities (pre-diabetes, dyslipidaemia, obesity, elevated BP) yet no assessment or plan was documented. Guidelines specify treatment goals of BP <140/90, FBG <7 mmol/L, and viral load suppression. Without a documented plan, there is risk of missed intervention for progressive metabolic syndrome and cardiovascular risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment and management plan addressing weight, glucose, lipids, and BP. Consider NCD integrated care referral and lifestyle counselling per guidelines.
